results.title: Brain region identification
results.question: What are the major subdivisions of the Drosophila mushroom body?
results.response: The major subdivisions of the Drosophila [mushroom body](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00005801 "Open mushroom body in Virtual Fly Brain") are the calyx, pedunculus, and mushroom body lobe system. This information comes from the VFB database, which describes the mushroom body as being divided into these three parts: the calyx, which receives sensory interneuron afferents; the pedunculus, a thick axon bundle extending from the calyx to the base of the lobes; and the mushroom body lobe system, consisting of a vertical branch and a medial branch with different structures at different life stages. VFB holds various data related to the mushroom body, including images, neuron information, parts, and subclasses, with specific counts available, such as [2](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00005801,ListAllAvailableImages "Run in VFB: List all available images of mushroom body") subclasses of mushroom body, [176](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00005801,PartsOf "Run in VFB: Parts of mushroom body") parts of mushroom body, and [602](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00005801,NeuronsPartHere "Run in VFB: Neurons with some part in mushroom body") neurons with some part in mushroom body.

results.title: Complete neuron profile
results.question: Give me a comprehensive profile of the giant fiber neuron: its anatomy, connectivity, available driver lines, and relevant publications.
results.response:
The [giant fiber neuron](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00004020 "Open giant fiber neuron in Virtual Fly Brain") is a large adult descending neuron that controls jump escape behavior, as recorded in VFB. According to VFB, it has specific anatomy, with its large cell body located posterior to the lower protocerebrum, and a large descending axon that is several times larger than any other axon in the cervical connective. This axon enters the cervical connective via the posterior cerebro-cervical fascicle and descends on the ipsilateral side, in the dorsal cervical fasciculus. The NBLAST similarity score is calculated by finding the closest tangent vector in the target neuron for each tangent vector in the query neuron, and then summing the scores from the distance between and the dotproduct of the two vectors, typically normalized to a self-self comparison with a perfect match being 1, as described in the documentation.
